review_reference: Owner decision Q64 of 2026-11-13 ("Q64 option A, sensitive excluded, DPO sign-off"): the patient chooses on the share, default off; sensitive classes excluded unless the patient opts in separately; break-glass never unlocks it; seal-aware; one audit row per read; release waits for DPO sign-off. To be signed by the owner.
evidence: Migration 0124_cross_facility_imports.sql (provisional number; ordered after 0123) plus its runtime-grants.sql block. WHAT IT DOES: a patient may choose, on a share, to also show their imported paper records (lab imports 0017, pharmacy imports 0023) from OTHER facilities to the share's clinician, and separately whether sensitive records (HIV/ARV, TB, psychiatric, sickle cell) are included. Default off: every existing share and every share made by invitation stays facility-only. New table identity.patient_share_scopes (one row per share that includes other facilities; immutable; forced RLS; owner-only policy; no runtime grant). New command identity.create_my_consent_share_scoped calls 0095's create_my_consent_share unchanged and writes the scope in the same transaction (a replay must name the same scope), with one count-only audit row; identity.list_my_share_scopes lists the patient's own. Reads lab.patient_imports_other_facilities and pharmacy.patient_imports_other_facilities (SECURITY DEFINER, owned by the import tables' owner, EXECUTE for the Lab or Pharmacy runtime and the schema-test runtime only) return a page of the patient's imports from other facilities only under an active patient share to the caller's own membership at the session facility with the scope chosen, purpose direct-care, never break-glass, a PIN grant or an approved request, and only when identity.has_active_consent_grant also allows read_records (deny directives, holds and inactive accounts refuse); only from source facilities on the patient's side of the seal (real, 0098 demo, 0123 QA when present); never entered-in-error lab imports; sensitive records withheld whole unless included (identity.cross_facility_text_sensitive: hid.ocr.sensitive/v2's lists widened with the patient-results policy's HIV, TB, psychiatric and sickle-cell fragments and Nigerian lab shorthand, applied to every text a read returns, including the external laboratory, its reference, units, ranges and the source facility's name). Each read writes one audit row (ids and counts only, never values); a refusal (no qualifying share) writes one count-only denied audit row (who, which patient, the reason code), kept because the function does not raise: it sets hid.other_facilities_refused and returns nothing, and the service answers 403 after commit. ROW-LEVEL SECURITY: the reads' owner bypasses neither superuser nor RLS in production (P8), so each read writes a row for its transaction and patient in lab/pharmacy .other_facility_import_reads just before and deletes it just after; new SELECT policies for that owner only (lab_imported_evidence_other_facilities, lab_imported_observations_other_facilities, pharmacy_imports_other_facilities) admit only the marked patient's rows while the marker exists (0119's pattern). No runtime role gains a read. NOT CHANGED: every existing body, policy, grant and the facility-scoped reads. LOCKS: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE NOWAIT on the three import tables for the policies, bounded at 5 s (else 55P03). Preconditions: the import tables' policies exactly 0017's and 0023's, forced RLS, one lab owner; post-checks: no runtime privilege on the new tables or helpers, the three new policies SELECT for one role. Proven with superuser and with a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (the new suite cross-facility-imports, and with the new policies removed the reads return nothing). Release waits for the DPO's sign-off of the data-protection note in the PR.
